Coach [Don Feeley](/wiki/Don_Feeley "Don Feeley"), formerly the basketball coach at [Fairleigh Dickinson University](/wiki/Fairleigh_Dickinson_University "Fairleigh Dickinson University") in [New Jersey](/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey"), traveled to Sudan to coach and held clinics for the Sudanese national team in 1982. Feeley convinced Bol to go to the United States and play basketball.[[19]](#cite_note-20)[[20]](#cite_note-auto1-21)

With Feeley's input, Bol first landed in [Cleveland](/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland"). According to [Cleveland State University](/wiki/Cleveland_State_University "Cleveland State University") basketball coach [Kevin Mackey](/wiki/Kevin_Mackey "Kevin Mackey"), Bol could not provide a record of his birth date.[[7]](#cite_note-Yahoo_Birthdate-8) Mackey listed it as October 16, 1962, on Cleveland State documents, making Bol 19 years old, but he believed Bol was actually much older, possibly as old as 35.[[7]](#cite_note-Yahoo_Birthdate-8) Bol did not speak or write English at the time of his arrival in Cleveland. He improved his English skills after months of classes at ESL Language Centers at [Case Western Reserve University](/wiki/Case_Western_Reserve_University "Case Western Reserve University"), but not enough to qualify for enrollment at Cleveland State. Bol never played a game for Cleveland State. Five years later, Cleveland State was placed on two years' probation for providing improper financial assistance to Bol and two other African players.[[21]](#cite_note-22)[[22]](#cite_note-auto2-23)

Again with Feeley's influence, Bol declared his intention to play professionally in the [National Basketball Association](/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). *Noble gas* is translated from the [German](/wiki/German_language "German language") noun *Edelgas*, first used in 1900 by [Hugo Erdmann](/wiki/Hugo_Erdmann "Hugo Erdmann")[[5]](#cite_note-5) to indicate their extremely low level of reactivity. The name makes an analogy to the term "[noble metals](/wiki/Noble_metal "Noble metal")", which also have low reactivity. The noble gases have also been referred to as *[inert gases](/wiki/Inert_gas "Inert gas")*, but this label is deprecated as many [noble gas compounds](/wiki/Noble_gas_compound "Noble gas compound") are now known.[[6]](#cite_note-6) *Rare gases* is another term that was used,[[7]](#cite_note-7) but this is also inaccurate because [argon](/wiki/Argon "Argon") forms a fairly considerable part (0.94% by volume, 1.3% by mass) of the [Earth's atmosphere](/wiki/Earth%27s_atmosphere "Earth's atmosphere") due to decay of radioactive [potassium-40](/wiki/Potassium-40 "Potassium-40").[[8]](#cite_note-8)

[![A line spectrum chart of the visible spectrum showing sharp lines on top.](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Helium_spectrum.jpg/330px-Helium_spectrum.jpg)](/wiki/File:Helium_spectrum.jpg)

Thanks to its characteristic [spectral lines](/wiki/Spectral_line "Spectral line"), [Helium](/wiki/Helium "Helium") was discovered to exist on the Sun before it was discovered on Earth.

[Pierre Janssen](/wiki/Pierre_Janssen "Pierre Janssen") and [Joseph Norman Lockyer](/wiki/Joseph_Norman_Lockyer "Joseph Norman Lockyer") had discovered a new element on 18 August 1868 while looking at the [chromosphere](/wiki/Chromosphere "Chromosphere") of the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun"), and named it [helium](/wiki/Helium "Helium") after the Greek word for the Sun, ἥλιος (*hḗlios*).[[9]](#cite_note-9) No chemical analysis was possible at the time, but helium was later found to be a noble gas. A WCRF panel report finds the evidence "convincing" that alcoholic drinks increase the risk of colorectal cancer in men at consumption levels above 30 grams of absolute alcohol daily.[[73]](#cite_note-WCRF-73) The [National Cancer Institute](/wiki/National_Cancer_Institute "National Cancer Institute") states, "Heavy alcohol use may also increase the risk of colorectal cancer"[[74]](#cite_note-74)

Main article: [macOS High Sierra](/wiki/MacOS_High_Sierra "MacOS High Sierra")

macOS 10.13 High Sierra was released to the public on September 25, 2017.[[224]](#cite_note-229) Like [OS X El Capitan](/wiki/OS_X_El_Capitan "OS X El Capitan") and [OS X Mountain Lion](/wiki/OS_X_Mountain_Lion "OS X Mountain Lion"), High Sierra is a refinement-based update having very few new features visible to the user, including updates to Safari, Photos, and Mail, among other changes.[[225]](#cite_note-:1-230)

The major change under the hood is the switch to the [Apple File System](/wiki/Apple_File_System "Apple File System"), optimized for the solid-state storage used in most new Mac computers.[[226]](#cite_note-231)
